# 05 — Deep configuration

## 1. Sources, precedence and restart [Community Build]

System properties are read at startup and not stored in the database. Channels, increasing precedence: `sonar.properties`, environment, command line (source: https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-community-build/server-installation/system-properties/configuration-methods.md). Env var: name uppercased, `.`/`-` → `_`, so `sonar.web.systemPasscode` → `SONAR_WEB_SYSTEMPASSCODE` (source: `sonar-application/src/main/assembly/conf/sonar.properties:8-12`).

`sonar.properties` is **not reloaded by `api/system/restart`**; it needs a full restart (source: `sonar-application/src/main/assembly/conf/sonar.properties:1-6`). The endpoint restarts web, search and CE, requires `Administer System`, standalone only (source: `server/sonar-webserver-webapi/src/main/java/org/sonar/server/platform/ws/RestartAction.java:54-68`).

Documented properties only: others raise a startup warning and may have no effect (source: https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-community-build/server-installation/system-properties/configuration-methods.md).

## 2. Web, HTTP and sessions [Community Build]

Defaults and bounds (source: `sonar-application/src/main/assembly/conf/sonar.properties:97-168`; https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-community-build/server-installation/system-properties/system-properties.md).

| Property | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `sonar.web.host` | `0.0.0.0` | listen IP; `127.0.0.1` behind a proxy |
| `sonar.web.port` | `9000` | inbound HTTP port |
| `sonar.web.context` | empty (root) | URL prefix, starts with `/` |
| `sonar.web.http.maxThreads` | `50` | accepted concurrent connections |
| `sonar.web.http.minThreads` | `5` | minimum threads |
| `sonar.web.http.acceptCount` | `25` | queue when all threads are busy |
| `sonar.web.http.keepAliveTimeout` | `60000` | ms per connection; `-1` = infinite |
| `sonar.web.http.maxPostSize` | `-1` | POST body bytes; `-1` = unlimited |
| `sonar.web.sessionTimeoutInMinutes` | `4320` (3 days) | idle session; 6…129600 |
| `sonar.web.activeSessionTimeoutInMinutes` | `129600` (90 days) | [Server: Enterprise+] active session; 15…129600 |
| `sonar.auth.jwtBase64Hs256Secret` | empty | Base64 HS256 key; sessions survive restart |
| `sonar.web.systemPasscode` | disabled | monitoring passcode in header `X-Sonar-Passcode` |

JWT secret: `echo -n "texto" | openssl dgst -sha256 -hmac "key" -binary | base64`, unique per installation (source: `sonar-application/src/main/assembly/conf/sonar.properties:139-144`).

## 3. JDBC pool [Community Build]

Rule: `maxActive` ≈ 1.2 × `sonar.web.http.maxThreads` (60) (source: `sonar-application/src/main/assembly/conf/sonar.properties:60-75`). Code defaults (source: `server/sonar-process/src/main/java/org/sonar/process/ProcessProperties.java:59-61`):

| Property | Default (code) | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `sonar.jdbc.maxActive` | `60` | simultaneous active connections |
| `sonar.jdbc.minIdle` | `10` | minimum idle connections |
| `sonar.jdbc.maxWait` | `8000` | ms to wait before an exception |

`sonar.jdbc.maxIdle` is deprecated and inert (source: `server/sonar-db-migration/src/main/java/org/sonar/db/DefaultDatabase.java:71-74`). The page https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-community-build/server-installation/system-properties/system-properties.md diverges (`minIdle=2`, `maxIdle=5`, `maxWait=5000`): trust the 26.12 code.

## 4. JVM: `javaOpts` × `javaAdditionalOpts` [Community Build]

`javaOpts` (web, CE, search) **replaces** all default flags; `javaAdditionalOpts` **appends** without dropping `-Xms`/`-Xmx`. With both, the second is appended to the first (source: https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-community-build/server-installation/system-properties/system-properties.md).

```properties
sonar.web.javaOpts=-Xmx2G -Xms1G -server
sonar.web.javaAdditionalOpts=-Djava.security.egd=file:/dev/./urandom
sonar.ce.javaAdditionalOpts=-Dcom.sun.management.jmxremote=true
sonar.search.javaOpts=-Xmx2G -Xms2G -XX:MaxDirectMemorySize=1G
```

     1	NAME
     2	podman-kube-apply - Apply Kubernetes YAML based on containers, pods, or volumes to a Kubernetes cluster
     3	SYNOPSIS
     4	podman kube apply [options] [container… | pod… | volume…]
     5	DESCRIPTION
     6	podman kube apply deploys a podman container, pod, or volume to a Kubernetes cluster. Use the --file option to deploy a Kubernetes YAML (v1 specification) to a Kubernetes cluster as well.
     7	Note that the Kubernetes YAML file can be used to run the deployment in Podman via podman-play-kube(1).
     8	OPTIONS
     9	--ca-cert-file=ca cert file path | “insecure”
    10	The path to the CA cert file for the Kubernetes cluster. Usually the kubeconfig has the CA cert file data and generate kube automatically picks that up if it is available in the kubeconfig. If no CA cert file data is available, set this to insecure to bypass the certificate verification.
    11	--file, -f=kube yaml filepath
    12	Path to the Kubernetes yaml file to deploy onto the Kubernetes cluster. This file can be generated using the podman kube generate command. The input may be in the form of a yaml file, or stdin. For stdin, use --file=-.
    13	--kubeconfig, -k=kubeconfig filepath
    14	Path to the kubeconfig file to be used when deploying the generated kube yaml to the Kubernetes cluster. The environment variable KUBECONFIG can be used to set the path for the kubeconfig file as well.
    15	Note: A kubeconfig can have multiple cluster configurations, but kube generate always picks the first cluster configuration in the given kubeconfig.
    16	--ns=namespace
    17	The namespace or project to deploy the workloads of the generated kube yaml to in the Kubernetes cluster.
    18	--service, -s
    19	Used to create a service for the corresponding container or pod being deployed to the cluster. In particular, if the container or pod has portmap bindings, the service specification includes a NodePort declaration to expose the service. A random port is assigned by Podman in the service specification that is deployed to the cluster.

     5	podman\-network.unit - systemd unit files for managing Podman networks using Quadlet
     6	
     7	# SYNOPSIS

    10	
    11	# DESCRIPTION
    12	
    13	Network files are named with a `.network` extension and contain a section `[Network]` describing the
    14	named Podman network. The generated service is a one-time command that ensures that the network
    15	exists on the host, creating it if needed.
    16	
    17	By default, the Podman network has the same name as the unit, but with a `systemd-` prefix, i.e. for
    18	a network file named `$NAME.network`, the generated Podman network is called `systemd-$NAME`, and
    19	the generated service file is `$NAME-network.service`. The `NetworkName` option allows for
    20	overriding this default name with a user-provided one.
    21	
    22	Please note that stopping the corresponding service will not remove the Podman network by default -
    23	this can be overridden by the `NetworkDeleteOnStop=true` option.
    24	
    25	In addition, updating an existing network is not supported.
    26	In order to update the network parameters, you must first manually remove the Podman network and then restart the service.
    27	
    28	Using network units allows containers to depend on networks being automatically pre-created. This is
    29	particularly interesting when using special options to control network creation, as Podman otherwise creates networks with the default options.

    31	# USAGE SUMMARY

    34	`.service` that runs `podman network create`.

**podman compose** is a thin wrapper around an external compose provider such as docker-compose or podman-compose.  This means that `podman compose` is executing another tool that implements the compose functionality but sets up the environment in a way to let the compose provider communicate transparently with the local Podman socket. ## Volume units [Volume]

Volume files are named with a `.volume` extension and contain a section `[Volume]` describing the
named Podman volume. The generated service is a one-time command that ensures that the volume
exists on the host, creating it if needed. Unlike `.network`, `.image`, and `.artifact` oneshot units,
the generated service for `.volume` units does not set `RemainAfterExit=yes` by default.

By default, the Podman volume has the same name as the unit, but with a `systemd-` prefix, i.e. for
a volume file named `$NAME.volume`, the generated Podman volume is called `systemd-$NAME`, and the
generated service file is `$NAME-volume.service`. The `VolumeName` option allows for overriding this
default name with a user-provided one.

Using volume units allows containers to depend on volumes being automatically pre-created. This is
particularly interesting when using special options to control volume creation,
as Podman otherwise creates volumes with the default options.

Valid options for `[Volume]` are listed below:

| **[Volume] options**                | **podman volume create equivalent**       |
|-------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|
| ContainersConfModule=/etc/nvd\.conf | --module=/etc/nvd\.conf                   |
